title: Albóndigas en Salsa
subtitle: Spanish meatballs in a saffron and tomato sauce
excerpt: Albóndigas en salsa are Spanish-style meatballs braised in a flavoured tomato sauce. Unlike Italian meatballs in tomato sauce, the Spanish version uses saffron, paprika, and sometimes sherry in the sauce, producing a richer, more aromatic result. Served with crusty bread or boiled potatoes.
sourceNotes: Albóndigas (meatballs) appear throughout Spanish and Mexican cooking. The Spanish word derives from the Arabic al-bunduqa (small ball), reflecting the Moorish culinary influence on Iberian cooking. Albóndigas en salsa are a standard dish in Spanish homes and bars, and appear as tapas in small earthenware dishes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce. Defrost overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales directly. Makes a good batch for freezing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better made the day before. The sauce absorbs into the meatballs overnight.

content.text: The saffron is what makes the Spanish albóndigas distinct from Italian polpette: steep the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of warm water for 10 minutes before adding to the sauce. The colour turns a deep gold and the aroma intensifies. Do not skip this step: adding dry saffron threads directly to the sauce releases very little flavour.

items.prepNote: 2 cloves for meatballs, 3 for the sauce

content.text: Make the meatballs: combine the beef mince, breadcrumbs, egg, 2 crushed garlic cloves, parsley, cumin, and a generous seasoning of salt and pepper. Mix well and roll into balls about 3 cm across (yields about 24). Dust lightly in flour.
Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in batches, turning, for 3 to 4 minutes until sealed on all sides. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan, add 1 tablespoon of oil and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add 3 garlic cloves and fry for 1 minute. Add the smoked paprika and the saffron with its soaking water. Stir for 30 seconds. Add the tinned tomatoes and 200 ml of water. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the sauce. Simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes until cooked through. Season with salt. Serve in the pan with bread or potatoes.

items.symptom: Meatballs fall apart in the sauce
items.cause: Not enough binder (egg or breadcrumbs), or meatballs were not browned before going into the sauce
items.fix: Browning the meatballs first creates a crust that holds them together during simmering. Make sure the meatball mixture is well mixed and the egg is evenly distributed.
